summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for several weeks of intermittent bloody, watery diarrhea and abdominal pain, with reported fevers at home. She denied recent travel but recalled eating shrimp a month prior. In the ED, she developed hypertension, managed with IV labetalol. Evaluation included a CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast due to allergy, which showed no acute intra-abdominal process but a nodular liver contour consistent with cirrhosis. A head CT showed no acute findings. She had no further bowel movements during admission, limiting stool studies. After discussion, she opted to continue work-up as an outpatient, and was provided with stool collection kits. Urine culture grew E. coli, but she was asymptomatic, so treatment was withheld. Her symptoms stabilized, and she was discharged home with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider if diarrhea recurred, monitor weight, and continue all chronic medications.
